text:
The U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments have released a detailed timeline of their Megaspeed investigation, confirming $NVDA stopped selling to the Singapore data-center company in June 2025, when it was placed on Nvidia's internal "no sell" list.

Here's what the joint statement reveals:

2024: Commerce opened an investigation after detecting suspicious activity suggesting possible diversion of sensitive U.S. semiconductors.

May 2025: Investigators requested Nvidia's records covering direct and indirect sales to Megaspeed.

June 2025: Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its internal "no sell" list.

June 2025: U.S. and Singaporean authorities conducted an on-site inspection of Megaspeed and interviewed its then-CEO, Alice Huang.

Afterward: The Justice Department took the lead in the criminal investigation.

The disclosure comes after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized Commerce for not placing Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist, despite support from four federal agencies.

Importantly, Nvidia's internal "no sell" list is separate from the government's Entity List.

Source: U.S. Commerce and Justice Departments

$TSM just posted its best month ever

October revenue: ~$17.9bn
• Up 59.7% from a year earlier
• Up 14.7% from September
• 14% above the previous record, set in August
• January–October revenue up 43.3%

Why it matters for Q4
TSMC guided Q4 to $52.3–54.3bn. October alone delivered about 34% of the midpoint.

To hit the midpoint, November and December need ~$17.7bn a month, to hit the top of the range, ~$18.2bn a month, analysts expected ~$16.4–17.4bn a month

8 optical engines/GPU introduces 100x more lasers than scale out switching. More conservative estimates were 10x laser content from AOI's CFO.

From what I've seen yearly capacity expansion for lasers generally increase around ~3x Y/Y like $AVGO projections, or ~5x over 2-3 years like Furukawa's.

Future CPO laser competitors like Furukawa/AOI/Shija are more nuanced, since AOI is focused on 800G/1.6T transceivers (which faced capacity expansion delays + DSP Bottlenecks), but they have capability for 400mW+ ranges + ongoing CPO qualifications. 

I don't think transceivers have the same durability though in capex reduction scenarios, which is why I've been arguing the valuable optionality AOI has to focus on merchant lasers is mispriced.

text:
Well, most of the time projections are noise and reactionary. 

Like right now, sky-high projections for $ANT $700-$800B ARR over next few years is stirring up hype that I'd argue gets revised down later. 

I do think it's important to model in capex forecasts dropping past 2028, due to the current reflexive nature of AI selloffs, rate hikes, etc. 

The drawn out duration of Iran War doesn't help, Jensen leaving $NVDA certainty draws concerns over Nvidia's ecosystem. 

But any catalyst, like if Iran War ends, can also change sentiment in a heartbeat (since bearish positioning is overwhelming). 

- It's also clear financing has been tightening, since OpenAI only managed to raise $11B of their original $30B target so far. 

- Markets are reacting enthusiastically to companies like $TE doing a $100M ATM today (nuking valuations)

There's also the obvious fact that Nvidia wants to sell chips to China for market share reasons whether or not Jensen is in bed with a spy or spy-adjacent person. It's not like he needs her to convince him. That's already their normal incentive unless they're outright blocked from doing so.

From a board perspective there is political pressure, but then also internal policy. If it's true he also slept with a subordinate without disclosure, it adds complications. And then as I mentioned in my first post: did he lie to the board in recent months?

One might argue the board acted too fast. One might argue he should come back. (I'm not necessarily against either of those with information at hand). But statements like, "His personal life is none of their business," are factually inaccurate here, since it's not an unrelated set of affairs. It's something the board *has* to look into and potentially (that's where it's up to dispute) take action on.
